$comment: How the BDD-only mutation run (stryker.bdd.config.mjs) is split across jobs. One unsharded run mutates every file in src/ against the BDD suite alone and does not finish: its first and only attempt was killed at 30 minutes (nightly-mutation.yml, 2026-09-17), so mutation-bdd-thresholds.json has never been seeded and no Rule has a mutation floor. Each shard here is a set of directories; nightly-mutation.yml runs one job per shard and merges the reports before the ratchet, so the gate still sees one score per directory.
$invariant: The shards partition src/: every TypeScript file under it belongs to exactly one shard. tests/tdd/mutation-ratchet/bddShards.test.ts fails on a file claimed twice or not at all, so a shard boundary cannot quietly drop a directory from the run. The exclusions in stryker.bdd.config.mjs apply to every shard alike, so the union of the shards mutates exactly what the unsharded glob did.
$balance: Balanced by mutant count, measured with `BDD_MUTATION_SHARD=<name> npx stryker run stryker.bdd.config.mjs --dryRunOnly`. src/core was one shard of 1,545 mutants until 2026-09-18; it is now three, because that one took longer than the rest of the matrix put together and a reclaimed runner costs the whole run (the merge refuses an incomplete set, by design). Per directory: requestPipeline 503, rateLimiter 401, pagination 231, circuitBreaker 193, cache 182, middleware 35 — giving core-request-pipeline 538, core-backoff 594, core-cache 413. Rebalance by moving a directory between shards; the partition test is what makes that safe.
